topic: Driving Safely: Vehicle Inspection & Basic Control
question: What is the minimum tread depth required in every major groove on the front tires of a commercial vehicle?
explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32-inch tread depth in every major groove; other tires need 2/32 inch.
source_note: Section 2.1.3 - What to Look For, Tire Problems

topic: Driving Safely: Vehicle Inspection & Basic Control
question: If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing in a leaf spring, what happens?
choice_a: Nothing, it is still considered safe
choice_b: The vehicle will be put out of service
choice_c: It only matters on the rear axle
choice_d: It requires a warning sticker only
explanation: If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing in a leaf spring, the vehicle will be put out of service; any defect could be dangerous.

topic: Driving Safely: Vehicle Inspection & Basic Control
question: During the engine start-up check, air pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within what time frame?
explanation: Air pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes; governor cut-out is usually around 120-140 psi.
source_note: Section 2.1.5 - Step 3: Start Engine and Inspect Inside the Cab

topic: Driving Safely: Vehicle Inspection & Basic Control
question: What does it mean if the dashboard ABS indicator light stays on after startup instead of turning off?
choice_b: The vehicle needs an oil change
choice_c: The parking brake is still engaged
choice_d: The ABS is not working properly
explanation: The ABS light should come on then turn off; if it stays on, the ABS is not working properly.
source_note: Section 2.1.5 - Step 3, Start Engine and Inspect Inside the Cab

topic: Driving Safely: Vehicle Inspection & Basic Control
question: How many red reflective warning triangles (or equivalent) must be carried as emergency equipment?
explanation: Warning devices include three reflective warning triangles, or 6 fusees, or 3 liquid burning flares.

topic: Driving Safely: Vehicle Inspection & Basic Control
question: For drivers of trucks and truck tractors transporting cargo, cargo securement must be inspected within the first 50 miles of a trip, and then how often afterward?
choice_b: Every 150 miles or 3 hours, whichever comes first
choice_c: Only at the end of the trip
explanation: Cargo securement must be inspected within the first 50 miles, then every 150 miles or every three hours, whichever comes first.
source_note: Section 2.1.6 - Inspection during a Trip, Safety Inspection

topic: Driving Safely: Vehicle Inspection & Basic Control
question: When backing a vehicle, which direction should you generally back and turn toward, and why?
choice_a: Toward the passenger side, because it's the legal requirement
choice_c: Toward the driver's side, because you can see better by looking out the side window
choice_d: Toward whichever side has more space, regardless of visibility
explanation: Backing toward the driver's side lets you watch the rear of the vehicle through the side window; backing toward the right is dangerous because visibility is worse.
source_note: Section 2.2.4 - Backing Safely, Back and Turn Toward the Driver's Side

topic: Driving Safely: Vehicle Inspection & Basic Control
question: When testing hydraulic brakes for leaks during a vehicle inspection, what should you do?
choice_a: There is no way to test hydraulic brakes before driving
choice_b: Drive at 55 mph and slam the brakes
choice_d: Pump the brake pedal three times, then apply firm pressure and hold for five seconds -- the pedal should not move
explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold firm pressure for five seconds; if the pedal moves, there may be a leak that must be fixed before driving.
source_note: Section 2.1.5 - Step 7, Test for Hydraulic Leaks

topic: Driving Safely: Vehicle Inspection & Basic Control
question: What is the basic method for shifting up in a manual transmission that requires double clutching?
choice_a: Release accelerator, push in clutch and shift to neutral simultaneously; release clutch; let engine/gears slow to the rpm for the next gear; push in clutch and shift to the higher gear; release clutch and press accelerator
choice_b: Simply move the gear shift while holding the accelerator steady
choice_c: Push the clutch in once and hold it through the entire shift
explanation: Double clutching requires shifting to neutral first, matching engine speed to the next gear, then engaging the higher gear.
source_note: Section 2.3.1 - Basic Method for Shifting Up

topic: Driving Safely: Vehicle Inspection & Basic Control
question: Before starting down a hill, what should a driver do regarding gear selection?
choice_a: Shift into neutral to coast down
choice_b: Downshift to a gear lower than the one required to climb the same hill, before starting down
choice_c: Stay in the highest gear to save fuel
choice_d: Gear selection doesn't matter if the brakes are in good condition
explanation: Downshift before starting down a hill to a gear usually lower than needed to climb the same hill, so brakes don't have to work as hard and overheat.
source_note: Section 2.3.1 - Special conditions where you should downshift, Before Starting Down a Hill

topic: Driving Safely: Vehicle Inspection & Basic Control
question: When should a driver turn off a retarder, according to the manual?
choice_b: Never; retarders should always stay on
choice_c: Whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow-covered, since it may cause the drive wheels to skid
explanation: When drive wheels have poor traction, the retarder may cause them to skid, so it should be turned off on wet, icy, or snow-covered roads.

topic: Driving Safely: Vehicle Inspection & Basic Control
question: About how far ahead should a good driver typically look while driving?
choice_b: Only as far as the vehicle directly in front
explanation: Most good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead -- about one block at lower speeds, about a quarter mile at highway speeds.
source_note: Section 2.4.1 - Seeing Ahead, How Far Ahead to Look

topic: Driving Safely: Vehicle Inspection & Basic Control
question: When should mirror adjustment be checked, and under what condition can it be checked accurately?
choice_a: Prior to the start of any trip, and only accurately when the trailer(s) are straight
choice_b: Only at the start of employment; trailer position doesn't matter
choice_d: Mirrors never need adjustment once set
explanation: Mirror adjustment should be checked before the start of any trip, and can only be checked accurately when the trailers are straight.
source_note: Section 2.4.2 - Seeing to the Sides and Rear, Mirror Adjustment
